page: Amazon Web Services m6g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) based on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz. Each physical core has a single hardware thread, providing dedicated execution without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). There are no GPUs or local storage devices attached to the configuration, meaning all persistence requires network-attached storage via EBS. Network performance baseline is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent baseline capabilities typical of early-generation 64-bit ARM cloud instances. Stress-ng single-core performance ranks in the average range at 1489.98, while multi-core throughput delivers 5934.04. Large-block uncached memory operations register at 71.14 GB/sec for reads and 34.79 GB/sec for writes, placing memory throughput in the middle 50% tier. However, Geekbench metrics (954 single-core and 3166 multi-core) and PassMark tests (overall CPU score of 2687.62) position the processor in the lower benchmark quartiles when executing compute-intensive tasks, such as gzip compression (19.78 GB/sec) and physics simulations.

The instance achieves steady operational efficiency for standard general-purpose workflows due to dedicated ARM cores without hyperthreading contention. While it lacks vector extensions like AVX-512 and shows limited capabilities for high-throughput machine learning inference or complex cryptographic processing, PassMark database operations hold an average score of 2587.75, and Redis reaches 4.48 million SET operations per second. The instance is suited for general application backends, mid-tier web serving, microservices, and relational database hosting where steady memory-to-core ratios are prioritized over raw single-thread compute peaks.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 4 dedicated 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache and a 1 Gbps network baseline. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations position the m6g.xlarge in the middle tiers for uncached memory bandwidth and database operations, though compute-heavy instruction benchmarks like PassMark and Geekbench rank in the lower quartiles. The hardware architecture offers consistent dedicated core execution without hyperthreading overhead, making the m6g.xlarge suitable for containerized microservices, standard web hosting, caching systems, and lightweight database management.
